program_name: Biotechnology for Human and Animal Health (BHAH)
teaching_language: English [uncertain] — The Department of Veterinary Medicine page and the official Manifesto of Studies both state the programme is 'delivered entirely in English' and list 'Language: English'. However, the central UNISS course catalogue page for the same programme lists 'Lingua del corso: Inglese Italiano' (course language: English, Italian) and, under 'Lingua/e ufficiali di insegnamento e di accertamento della preparazione' (official language(s) of teaching and of assessment), states 'ITALIANO, INGLESE'. The pre-research also observed an Italian-titled 3 CFU food-safety course in the curriculum. Practical reading: the programme is run as an international English-taught degree (thesis must be written in English, entry interview is in English), but the central catalogue formally registers Italian alongside English, so one or more minor modules may be delivered or examinable in Italian.
campus: Sassari — Department of Veterinary Medicine (Dipartimento di Medicina Veterinaria), via Vienna 2, 07100 Sassari, Italy. This is the main Sassari campus, not Alghero/Olbia/Nuoro/Oristano.
degree_class: LM-9 — Biotecnologie mediche, veterinarie e farmaceutiche (Medical, Veterinary and Pharmaceutical Biotechnologies). The central UNISS catalogue records the class code as 'LM-9-R' (the reformed/'R' variant of LM-9). Duration 2 years, 120 ECTS, conventional (in-person) delivery mode, no compulsory attendance requirement.
admission_type: Open access ('Access: Free' / 'Tipologia di accesso: Libero') with a compulsory entry competency assessment. There is no numerus clausus ranking and no fixed number of places published for the programme, but admission is not automatic: every candidate must pass an 'entry competency test' verifying academic preparation before enrolment can be completed. The official wording is: 'The Master's Degree Program in Biotechnology for Human and Animal Health is an open-access program. To be admitted to a Master's Degree Program, candidates must: Hold a Bachelor's degree or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable under current regulations... Pass the entry competency test to verify their academic preparation.' No programme-specific non-EU quota cap was published on either the department page or the central catalogue page [uncertain]; at university level, visa-requiring international students are enrolled 'within the quota of places reserved for each study program according to the type of access provided (national or local programmed access)', which for an open-access programme implies no separate hard cap, but this was not confirmed by a programme-specific quota table.
academic_requirements: Accepted Italian bachelor degree classes (direct admission): L-2 (Biotecnologie / Biotechnology) and the former class 1; L-13 (Scienze Biologiche / Biological Sciences) and the former class 12; SNT/3 (bachelor's degree qualifying for the health profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician). Graduates of OTHER degree classes may also be admitted, 'subject to verification of the knowledge required to successfully follow the program'. International applicants: 'International applicants are welcome and will be admitted following an evaluation of their academic records, to ensure equivalence and alignment with the program's entry requirements' — i.e. a foreign bachelor's degree is assessed for equivalence to the above classes rather than being matched to a fixed ECTS table. NO minimum ECTS/CFU thresholds per subject area (no SSD-by-SSD credit minimums) are published for this programme on the department page, the central catalogue page, or the Manifesto of Studies 2025-26 [uncertain] — the subject-matter check is performed through the entry competency test instead. ENTRY ASSESSMENT FORMAT (this is the decisive step, not a diagnostic-only test): 'All candidates undergo an assessment of their academic preparation, which will consist of either a multiple-choice test or an individual interview.' In the operational instructions the two parts are described together: 'Take the test on the chosen date. Test topics: cytology, biochemistry, molecular biology, and cytogenetics and an English interview.' So the process is two-part in practice — a multiple-choice academic test covering cytology, biochemistry, molecular biology and cytogenetics, plus an interview conducted in English (which also serves as the English proficiency check when no certificate is presented). Both are held online. Candidates must also hold (or conditionally be about to hold) a bachelor's degree, and must pre-enrol via the SelfStudenti Uniss / Esse3 portal within the registration window of the test date they choose. Prerequisite bachelor degree completion: applicants still enrolled in a bachelor's programme in a.y. 2025/2026 who will graduate by December 2026 may enrol conditionally (see application_deadline_eu). Non-EU applicants requiring a visa additionally go through the national Universitaly pre-enrolment channel and the Italian diplomatic representation.
language_requirements: English at CEFR B2 level is mandatory. Official wording: 'A B2 level of English proficiency is also required, demonstrated by an internationally recognized certificate, equivalent university coursework, or assessed during the personal preparation evaluation.' (Italian catalogue version: 'È inoltre obbligatorio dimostrare una conoscenza della lingua inglese di livello B2, certificata attraverso attestazioni internazionali, il superamento di corsi universitari equivalenti, o mediante la verifica nel corso della valutazione della preparazione personale.') Three alternative routes of proof are therefore accepted: (1) an internationally recognised certificate, (2) equivalent university coursework already completed, or (3) direct assessment during the English interview that forms part of the entry competency test — meaning a candidate WITHOUT any certificate can still qualify by passing the English interview. THERE IS NO PUBLISHED FIXED SCORE TABLE: UNISS does not publish an IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge minimum-score list for this programme; no specific certificate names or numeric thresholds appear on the department page, the central catalogue page, or the Manifesto of Studies. Italian language: not required for admission to this programme itself; however, a separate university-level rule states that non-EU citizens who apply for full RECOGNITION of a foreign academic qualification (a different procedure from ordinary admission) must demonstrate Italian language proficiency.
application_deadline_eu: For a.y. 2026/2027 there is NO single application deadline — admission runs through four entry competency test rounds, each with its own registration window (all dates as published for a.y. 2026-27): Round 1 — test on 2026-03-05, registrations open 2026-02-05 to 2026-03-03. Round 2 — test on 2026-05-05, registrations open 2026-03-09 to 2026-05-03. Round 3 — test on 2026-07-01, registrations open 2026-05-06 to 2026-06-29. Round 4 — test on 2026-09-24, registrations open 2026-07-04 to 2026-09-22. As of the research date (2026-09-05) only Round 4 is still open. The page introduces these as 'The next dates for the competence assessment test', so additional autumn/winter 2026 rounds may be added later — in a.y. 2025/2026 the equivalent list ran to five rounds ending 2025-12-17 [uncertain]. CONDITIONAL ENROLMENT RULE: 'Students enrolled in a Bachelor's degree program during the 2025/2026 academic year who will graduate by December 2026 may also enroll conditionally.' — i.e. an applicant who has not yet graduated can sit the test and enrol conditionally provided the bachelor's degree is completed by December 2026. ENROLMENT FINALISATION: after passing the test the candidate completes online enrolment via the Uniss portal and pays through PagoPA; 'Enrollment is considered finalized only after the University has received the first installment of tuition fees.' At university level the general deadline for enrolling in master's degrees for graduates has historically been 15 January of the academic year (published as 'January 15, 2024: Deadline for enrollment in Master's Degrees for graduates, at Uniss or other Universities' on the UNISS Deadlines page) — but that page was last updated for a.y. 2023/2024 and the equivalent 2026/2027 date is not confirmed [uncertain].
application_deadline_non_eu: The same four 2026/2027 entry competency test rounds and registration windows apply to non-EU candidates (test 2026-03-05, reg. 2026-02-05→2026-03-03; test 2026-05-05, reg. 2026-03-09→2026-05-03; test 2026-07-01, reg. 2026-05-06→2026-06-29; test 2026-09-24, reg. 2026-07-04→2026-09-22), and the same conditional-enrolment rule applies (bachelor's degree to be completed by December 2026). No separate non-EU application deadline is published on the programme page [uncertain]. ADDITIONAL UNIVERSITALY / VISA STEP — YES, this exists and is separate: non-EU citizens residing abroad who need an entry visa must, before enrolment, submit a pre-enrolment application electronically through the UNIVERSITALY portal (universitaly.it) and then to the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate, within the deadlines set annually by the Italian Ministry (MUR/MAECI) in the 'Procedure per l'ingresso, il soggiorno e l'immatricolazione degli studenti richiedenti visto' provisions. The UNISS 'Enrollment for Non-EU Students' page states: 'If you are a non-EU citizen residing abroad and wish to study at the University of Sassari, you must first submit the pre-registration application to the Italian Representation within the deadlines set by the Ministry.' NOTE: that UNISS page is badly out of date — it still cites the a.y. 2024/2025 interministerial provisions and a visa-completion deadline of '30 November 2023'; the corresponding 2026/2027 Universitaly window and visa cut-off must be verified against the current ministerial decree and the Italian consulate [uncertain]. Exemption from the visa quota/pre-enrolment route: EU citizens (residing anywhere), Italian citizens holding a foreign qualification, and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy (art. 39 c.5 D.Lgs. 286/1998 as amended by art. 26 L. 189/2002) 'access university courses without quota limitations and apply for enrollment directly according to the procedures and deadlines established by the bachelor's or master's degree programs' — i.e. they follow only the four test rounds above. Reserved-place international schemes the University participates in include the 'Marco Polo' project (Chinese citizens) and the 'Formed' project (Maghreb area students).
required_documents: No programme-specific checklist of application documents is published by the Department of Veterinary Medicine [uncertain]. What is explicitly required by the published procedure: (1) registration of personal data on the SelfStudenti Uniss / Esse3 portal (http://uniss.esse3.cineca.it/Home.do); (2) online pre-enrolment through the same portal, selecting the Master's Degree Programme in Biotechnology for Human and Animal Health, within the chosen test round's registration window; (3) academic records / bachelor's degree transcript and qualification for the equivalence evaluation of international applicants ('admitted following an evaluation of their academic records, to ensure equivalence and alignment with the program's entry requirements'); (4) evidence of English at B2 — either an internationally recognised certificate or documentation of equivalent university coursework (not needed if English is assessed at the interview); (5) ISEE attestation (or authorisation for UNISS to retrieve DSU/ISEE data from INPS) if the applicant wants an income-based fee reduction — without it the maximum fee bracket is automatically applied; (6) proof of payment of the first tuition instalment via PagoPA, which finalises enrolment. For non-EU visa applicants, additionally: the Universitaly pre-enrolment application plus the documents required by the Italian Embassy/Consulate. For the separate procedure of formal recognition of a foreign academic qualification, UNISS requires (as PDFs): the secondary-school diploma valid for university admission in the issuing country; an official Italian translation of any document not issued in English; a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore) on the secondary-school diploma issued by the Italian diplomatic/consular representation; and the academic qualification to be recognised, likewise with official translation and Declaration of Value, or alternatively with a statement issued by the Italian ENIC-NARIC centre (CIMEA). Paper submission of the enrolment application to the Student Office is no longer required; candidates are advised to keep a PDF copy of the pre-enrolment.
entry_exam_or_test: YES — a compulsory 'entry competency test' (prova di verifica delle conoscenze) that every candidate must pass; it is decisive for admission, not merely diagnostic. FORMAT: two components in one online session — (a) a multiple-choice written test on cytology, biochemistry, molecular biology and cytogenetics, and (b) an individual interview conducted in English (which doubles as the B2 English check when no certificate is submitted). The formal regulation wording allows either modality: 'All candidates undergo an assessment of their academic preparation, which will consist of either a multiple-choice test or an individual interview' (Italian: 'La preparazione di ogni candidato sarà valutata tramite una prova scritta con quiz a risposta multipla o un colloquio individuale'), while the operational instructions describe both together: 'Take the test on the chosen date. Test topics: cytology, biochemistry, molecular biology, and cytogenetics and an English interview.' MODE: fully online — 'The test will be held ONLINE. The Microsoft Teams class code required to access the test will be sent to participants a day before the test.' No travel to Sassari is needed to sit it. ALL PUBLISHED ROUNDS FOR A.Y. 2026/2027 (four dates, each with its own registration window): 2026-03-05 (registrations 2026-02-05 → 2026-03-03); 2026-05-05 (registrations 2026-03-09 → 2026-05-03); 2026-07-01 (registrations 2026-05-06 → 2026-06-29); 2026-09-24 (registrations 2026-07-04 → 2026-09-22). FOR REFERENCE, the five rounds published for the previous cycle a.y. 2025/2026 were: 2025-09-26 (registrations until 2025-09-24), 2025-10-16 (registrations 2025-09-29 → 2025-10-14), 2025-11-06 (registrations 2025-10-20 → 2025-11-04), 2025-11-27 (registrations 2025-11-11 → 2025-11-25) and 2025-12-17 (registrations 2025-12-02 → 2025-12-15). Because the 2025/26 cycle ran rounds into December, further autumn 2026 rounds may still be added to the 2026/27 list [uncertain]. REGISTRATION MECHANICS: register on SelfStudenti Uniss (http://uniss.esse3.cineca.it/Home.do), pre-enrol online selecting this programme according to the registration schedule, then sit the test on the chosen date. There is no application fee published for the test itself [uncertain].
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.uniss.it/en/teaching/student-services/guide-studenti/tuition-fees-and-isee (English) — Italian equivalent under /it/didattica/servizi-agli-studenti/guide-studenti/. SUMMARY: UNISS charges a single income-related enrolment fee ('contributo unico'), quantified on the basis of the family unit's ISEE indicator, plus a €16.00 virtual stamp duty and the regional ERSU right-to-study tax. The fee is split into three instalments: a first instalment of variable amount up to approximately €310.00 (payable around 20 October, together with the €16 stamp duty), a second instalment (payable around end of February, together with the ERSU regional tax), and a third balancing instalment (payable around mid-April). FULL EXEMPTION ('no tax area'): students in the first year whose family ISEE is at or below €22,000 pay no enrolment fee (only the stamp duty and, if due, the ERSU tax); for later years the same ISEE threshold applies together with merit/ECTS conditions (at least 10, or 25, ECTS earned in the reference window depending on year of enrolment). Students who do not submit an ISEE/DSU or do not authorise UNISS to retrieve it from INPS are automatically placed in the HIGHEST income bracket and pay the maximum fee — a common trap for international students who cannot easily obtain an Italian ISEE. Payment is exclusively via PagoPA (https://www.uniss.it/it/didattica/servizi-agli-studenti/guide-studenti/pagopa); enrolment is finalised only once the first instalment is received. SCHOLARSHIPS: UNISS does not advertise its own dedicated scholarship for this programme; financial support is routed to the regional right-to-study body ERSU Sassari (scholarship and housing call), whose beneficiaries and eligible non-beneficiaries are exempt from the single enrolment fee, plus national/international schemes (MAECI, Erasmus+ for mobility) [uncertain]. EXACT 2026/2027 BRACKET AMOUNTS AND MAXIMUM ANNUAL FEE ARE NOT CONFIRMED — the accessible archived version of the fees page still carries a.y. 2023/2024 figures and deadlines [uncertain].

uncertainty_notes: ACADEMIC YEAR OF DATA: admission calendar, conditional-enrolment rule and entry-test format are taken from the a.y. 2026/2027 section explicitly published by the Department of Veterinary Medicine ('ENTRY COMPETENCY TEST FOR THE MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAM - A.Y. 2026-27'), so this is current-cycle data, not carried over from 2025/26. The Manifesto of Studies PDF linked from that page, however, is still the 2025-26 edition — a 2026-27 manifesto had not been published at the time of research. The central UNISS catalogue page content is from the 2025/26 catalogue snapshot. Tuition, deadline and non-EU pages at university level are considerably older (2023/24 and 2024/25 content) and their figures must not be treated as 2026/27 amounts. ACCESS METHOD: www.uniss.it and veterinaria.uniss.it are behind an AWS WAF 'Human Verification' interstitial that returns HTTP 405 to automated requests; all live fetches failed, so every source was read through Internet Archive Wayback Machine snapshots of the official pages (department English page 2026-06-10 and 2025-11-10; department Italian page and the fees/deadlines/non-EU/recognition pages via 2026-09 and 2026-03 captures; the Manifesto PDF via Wayback). No third-party aggregator was used as a source. A general web search independently returned the same four 2026/27 test dates, corroborating the archived content. OPEN UNCERTAINTIES: (1) Teaching language — department page and Manifesto say 'entirely in English', but the central catalogue registers ITALIAN and ENGLISH as official languages of teaching and assessment, and an Italian-titled 3 CFU food-safety module appears in the curriculum; the practical extent of Italian-language content is unresolved. (2) The 2026/27 round list may not be final — the page phrases them as 'the next dates', and the 2025/26 cycle ran five rounds through 17 December 2025, so additional autumn/winter 2026 rounds could be added after the 24 September 2026 sitting; as of the research date (2026-09-05) only the fourth round remains open. (3) No programme-specific non-EU quota figure was found on any official page. (4) No minimum ECTS/CFU thresholds per subject area are published; the entry test substitutes for a credit audit. (5) No IELTS/TOEFL score table is published anywhere for this programme — 'no fixed certificate score table exists' is the accurate statement. (6) No explicit programme-level document checklist is published; the document list given here is assembled from the enrolment procedure plus university-level rules on foreign-qualification recognition. (7) The 2026/2027 Universitaly pre-enrolment window and visa cut-off date are not stated on any UNISS page (the non-EU page still cites a 2023 visa deadline) and must be checked against the current ministerial decree. (8) The exact 2026/27 fee brackets, maximum annual contribution and instalment due dates are not confirmed. (9) No test/application fee is mentioned for the entry competency test, but its absence is not explicitly confirmed. (10) The programme is recent — it did not appear in the March 2025 English departmental listing and first appears in later captures, consistent with a 2025/26 launch; a first-cohort programme's procedures may change year to year.
